Chapter 10: Coming Home to Yourself — The Ongoing Journey
You know, there’s this quiet moment—often when you least expect it—where you suddenly realize that searching for love has always been about something much deeper. It’s really a longing to come home to yourself.
Healing isn’t about landing the perfect partner or pretending pain never existed. It’s about finding your way back to who you truly are, and choosing to live from that place.
Most of us, for years, look outside ourselves—craving validation, hunting for security, wanting to belong. That urge? It’s natural. We pick it up early on, shaped by those first experiences of connection and loss. But then, slowly, something shifts. You start to see that nobody else can patch up the spaces old wounds have left behind. Healing—real, lasting healing—is something only you can do for yourself.
Picture this: there’s a woman, who for decades, chased approval from everyone around her. One day, she just stopped. She began to notice the little ways she’d left herself behind—agreeing to things when she meant no, ignoring her own needs, swallowing her words. Instead of judging herself, she got curious. What if she chose differently? She started to speak up. Set some boundaries. Treated her feelings with respect. And you know what happened? The world didn’t fall apart. Actually, her relationships deepened, and she found a new sense of peace inside.
Coming home to yourself isn’t a one-time event—it’s a daily practice. It means tuning in to what you truly need, showing kindness to your own pain, and celebrating even the smallest steps forward. You don’t have to be perfect. You don’t have to never feel lonely. It’s really about knowing, deep down, that you are enough—just as you are.
The journey keeps going, with all its twists, doubts, and old patterns that sometimes sneak back in. But each time you return to yourself, it gets a little easier. And then it hits you: you are the one you’ve been waiting for all along.
